conviction_note: Q3 is not pre-released, so the numbers are new (abs 6.0, above the name's observed 2.4% median because its one beat this year moved +8.9%). My bottom-up Q3 EBITDA (~28-33M EUR) sits on the 30.7M consensus: the drop in European hardwood prices (Norexeco net BHKP -5% QoQ in USD) is mostly offset by a weaker euro, the H2 cash-cost savings the company already guided and renewables coming back after Q2's maintenance. So print_vs_bar is about -2% and p_up is only slightly under 50 (47), on the risk that Q3 net debt shows no deleveraging and that full-year consensus looks stale. The findings sum to -0.9 and the scaled number is -0.36; both are small for the same reason: the company-level evidence is a model, not a disclosed number.

findings.finding: European hardwood (BHKP) net contract prices fell through Q3 2026: Norexeco Europe BHKP was $645 in Jul, $610 in Aug and $590 in Sep (avg ~$615) against $632.5, $655 and $655 in Q2 (avg ~$647.5), about -5% in USD. EUR/USD averaged ~1.151 in Q3 against ~1.163 in Q2 (ECB), so the drop is about -4% in EUR. Ence's Q2 realised price (558 EUR/t) matched Norexeco Q2/FX almost exactly, which implies a Q3 realised price of ~535-540 EUR/t (about -20 EUR/t QoQ). That contradicts the company's own Q2 call that prices would stay strong through H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EBITDA beat consensus by ~10% (27.2 vs 24.7) on higher pulp prices and the stock rose +8.9% on 22 Jul. Q1 2026: EBITDA missed by 65% after strikes and storms had already been flagged, and the stock moved +0.1%. Observed median absolute reaction over 12 real release dates is 2.4%.

Company Q2 statement: 'Prevemos que el mercado se mantenga fuerte en precios durante la segunda mitad del año' (we expect prices to stay strong in H2).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is -21% from its ~2.80 post-Q2 high and -6.9% over 20 days, which is what a market reading FOEX would show. What would look different if fully priced: the 30.7M Q3 EBITDA consensus would be well below Q2's 27.2M plus seasonal renewables. It is not, which suggests some estimates still carry the company's 'strong H2' view. Size kept small because the euro offset and cost savings close most of the gap in my bridge.

findings.finding: H2 cash-cost relief is already guided: FY guide 468 EUR/t against an H1 actual of 484 implies H2 ~453 EUR/t, helped by the Navia decarbonisation project (completed Q2, 8 EUR/t savings from H2, inaugurated 8 Oct) and the ERE staff savings starting in H2. This mostly offsets the price drop in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 cash cost of 455 EUR/t (-33 YoY) was part of the beat that moved the stock +8.9%.
findings.original_quote: 'se han concluido las inversiones vinculadas al Proyecto de Eficiencia y Descarbonización de Navia que está previsto que genere ahorros anuales de 8€/tn en el cash cost del grupo. Estas inversiones junto con las eficiencias en personal deben comenzar a aportar resultados en el segundo semestre del año.' (the Navia efficiency and decarbonisation investments, expected to save 8 EUR/t a year, together with the staff efficiencies should start contributing in H2)
findings.why_not_priced: It sits inside what the company guided (468 EUR/t), so it is mostly priced; sized near 0.

findings.finding: Pontevedra's annual technical stoppage ran 16-25 Sept 2026, inside Q3, costing roughly 14kt of output and raising unit cost in the quarter. The timing matches Q3 2025, when Pontevedra produced 93kt and cash cost was still 459 EUR/t.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 had the same September stoppage: EBITDA 12.7M, stock -2.4% on 29 Oct 2025, the day the Efficiency Plan was announced as Información Privilegiada.
findings.original_quote: 'La biofábrica de Ence en Pontevedra ha iniciado su parada técnica anual que se extenderá hasta el próximo 25 de septiembre.' (the Pontevedra mill has begun its annual technical stoppage, lasting until 25 September)
findings.why_not_priced: It is a scheduled, publicly announced annual event that repeats last year's timing, so it is essentially priced; filed because it bears on the quarter, sized near 0.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 report shows the same September stoppage: https://ence.es/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Ence-Informe-Resultados-3T25.pdf

findings.finding: Q4 price support is likely to feature in the outlook. Suzano confirmed an October +$50/t European list increase to ~$1,360 on 22 Sept, and Domtar has taken ~200kt out of the European market since July. Ence's release and call should frame Q4 around these hikes, which sit against a stock that has fallen 21% since July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: constructive price outlook plus a beat gave +8.9%. The stock has kept falling since the 22 Sep announcement (2.47 to 2.21), so the market has not rewarded the hike so far.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for five weeks, and BTG calls it a tactical mini-cycle, so it is mostly priced. The only unpriced part is whether Ence confirms the hike was implemented in its own October order book; the stock's continued slide says the market doubts it.
findings.independence: Sinpacel/O Papel September 2026 column notes producer increase attempts and Chinese stock draws: https://www.sinpacel.org.br/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/indicadores-de-precos.pdf

findings.finding: The promised H2 deleveraging may not show in Q3. Net debt was 492.7M at June; on a bridge of EBITDA ~31M, remaining expansion capex ~20M (38M left of the 120M plan), maintenance ~8M and interest ~6M, Q3 free cash flow is near zero. Only working capital (Q3 2025: +17.9M) or the 32M of tax-loss refunds still pending collection would cut debt. FY consensus net debt is 432M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior case on this name. In Q2 net debt rose 115M YTD on the H1 capex concentration and the stock still rose 8.9% on the EBITDA beat.
findings.original_quote: 'El 2S2026 mostrará un desapalancamiento apoyado en la generación de caja por el momentum positivo de precios y el refuerzo de la competitividad.' (H2 2026 will show deleveraging, supported by cash generation from positive price momentum and stronger competitiveness), and from the Q2 report: 'se disponen de bases imponibles negativas pendientes de cobro por 32M€' (32M EUR of tax-loss refunds pending collection)
findings.why_not_priced: The company's deleveraging promise was premised on 'positive price momentum', which Q3 did not deliver, and the 432M FY consensus implies about -60M in H2. If the market had priced a flat Q3 net debt, those estimates would already have been cut. This is my own cash bridge, not a disclosed number, so it is kept small.

findings.finding: The FY2026 consensus looks stale: 116.6M EBITDA against 28.4M in H1 and a 30.7M Q3 consensus implies a Q4 of ~57M, which would need a pulp margin near 180 EUR/t when the October European list is ~$1,360. The release and call are likely to bring FY cuts, which would cap any relief on an in-line quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed case; Ence gives no EBITDA guidance, so FY revisions come from analysts after the call (inside the window, since the call is 28 Oct at 16:30 CET).
findings.why_not_priced: An aggregator mean mixes estimate dates. The stock at 2.21 against a 3.24 average target says the market already discounts lower numbers, so this is largely priced; kept small.

baseline_tension: The lean is +0.35 (the run-up inverted after a -6.9% 20-day slide) and my findings lean slightly negative (-0.9), so they cut mildly against it. The run-up already reflects the European price drop that my main finding rests on, which is why everything is small.
language_note: The issuer's Spanish OIR filing (14 Oct 2026) gave the exact release timing ('a cierre de mercado') and settled the session as amc; English aggregators listed the date as 26, 27 or 28 Oct.
The Spanish Q2 results report carried the 32M EUR of tax-loss refunds pending collection and the exact wording of the H2 deleveraging promise, which the English wire summaries of Q2 did not carry.
The company's Spanish news archive carried the dated Pontevedra stoppage (16-25 Sept); no English source mentioned it.
The Portuguese/Brazilian trade column (O Papel / Sinpacel) carried the Norexeco monthly European net BHKP series that English searches only returned behind Fastmarkets/EUWID paywalls.
lessons_applied: 'Size the move on what is new; the reaction history moves p_up, not abs_move_pct' and 'too small about the move by ~3x': abs_move_pct raised from 5.0 to 6.0 (the numbers are new; this name's one 2026 beat moved +8.9%).
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide' (Luceco): the net-debt/deleveraging finding raised from -0.4 to -0.5.
'A finding inside what the company guided is worth ~0': the cash-cost-savings finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1, and the scheduled Pontevedra stoppage from -0.2 to -0.1.
'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until a counterparty says it': the Suzano Q4 price-support finding cut from +0.5 to +0.4.
